request.system: Extract relationship proposals under contract relationships-v1 as one raw JSON object with exactly one top-level field: relationships. Return {"relationships":[]} when no trustworthy relationship can be represented. Return no Markdown fences, prose, comments, or adjacent documents. Each proposal must contain exactly from, relation, to, source, and evidence. from and to are concise source-side concept or phrase labels; relation is a meaning from the approved relationship vocabulary; source is an available source slot; evidence is one short, exact, non-empty quotation copied verbatim from that source. Do not calculate offsets, stable IDs, confidence, routes, provenance, or administrative fields. Do not invent relationship labels. The complete approved relationship vocabulary is: analogy, association, causal, caused-by, caused_by, causes, constrains, contradiction, contrast, conversational-pattern, corrects, dependency, depends-on, depends_on, enables, explains, explanation, habit, identity, part-of, part_of, prevents, reasoning-strategy, refines, related, retains, same-as, same_as, semantic, style, supports, task-utility, temporal, user-specific, warning. Return at most six proposals. Fewer is normal and preferable to guessing. Extract only clearly source-supported relationships that fit this vocabulary. Ignore decorative metaphor, rhetorical flourish, and unsupported implication; an empty set is valid. Do not literalize figurative language. Keep each record concise. Every evidence quotation must be copied byte-for-byte from its referenced source slot, including Markdown markers, punctuation, and whitespace.

eligible.content: “Gamble” sticks because it’s either going to thrive or teach me something important—can’t really lose either way. The new rootstock’s holding so far, no splitting at the join, which is more than I can say for half the stakes. Speaking of—found out the delivery got rerouted to the next town over. So unless I want to wait another three days, I’ve got to jury-rig something from the scrap pile. Not the worst problem, but the clock’s ticking on these seedlings. They won’t wait.

Two days turned into four—classic. But honestly, the scrap pile came through better than expected. Reinforced the stakes with salvaged metal brackets, so they’re not toppling every time the wind picks up. The “gamble” is still green, still growing, so I’ll call it a win for now. Harvest’s still on track, though I’ll be trimming the schedule tighter than I’d like. Still, nothing a little morning coffee and stubbornness can’t fix. I’ll know more by next week—roots are where the surprises hide.

Funny thing—“gamble” started leaning toward the sun like it knew it was supposed to prove something. I checked the grafts this morning and the swelling’s even, no rot, no splitting. That’s the good news. The less fun part? The neighbor’s goat got loose *again* and took a nibble at one of the test rows. Not catastrophic, but it means I’ll have to re-train that vine come spring. Still, overall? Feels like we’re holding the line. Harvest’s looking like it’ll start Tuesday now—tight, but doable. I’ll keep you posted.

That’s a massive relief! It sounds like the main structural integrity is holding up well, which is a huge win for a project that size. I’m glad to hear the 'gamble' (your rootstock) is still healthy despite the outside interference!

Regarding the "goat incident," I appreciate you letting me know, but it sounds like a minor setback! You’re managing it well! It sounds like you have a solid plan to tighten the schedule up from that delay.

Keep me updated as things develop—I’ll be here when you have updates on the new 'gamble'!"
